title: EPIC CR-1: one-market continuous runtime
description:
CR-1 means one operator-selected active-program market at S=12 may repeat
maker-entry, reduction, flat and requote cycles without synchronous operator
involvement during one declared market assignment. It runs under launchd and
caffeinate, survives process and websocket restarts through safe adoption, and
either continues safely or durably enters WINDING_DOWN while reduction,
monitoring, heartbeat and alert retry remain alive.

The closed operating envelope is: one selected ticker; dedicated account with
only declared capital and no unrelated cash, positions, orders or manual
activity; manual market replacement; no claim of automatic programme rotation.
Required evidence is a green read-only qualification, clean S=1 first-fill
canary, clean attended S=12 burn-in, final scenario/invariant and operational
readiness, exact full promotion gate, active external dead man, and explicit
operator review.

New work blocks CR-1 only after adjudication that its failure is reachable in
this operating envelope or that CR-1 acceptance cannot be evidenced without it.
Priority labels alone do not move the finish line. Dynamic selection, rotation
and automatic management of unrelated held markets belong to CR-2; CR-1 instead
refuses a dirty account and stops on foreign activity.

Acceptance: record exact commit, config/rung, assignment window, dedicated-
account check, supervision state, runbook/drill evidence and links to all three
promotion rungs. After closure, repeated cycles are authorised only inside that
assignment.

title: H-Q-4a: sustained gate-failure cancel and sweep
description:
`cfg.Params.GateFailDebounce` is configured and tested but has no production
reader. The owner publishes book qualification as telemetry, yet H-Q-4a's
response never occurs: after 30 seconds of a non-qualifying book, adding orders
remain live and fillable while the interval earns no reward.

Implement a per-market, monotonic continuous-failure interval from accepted,
current-generation book state. Before the debounce expires, place no new order
from a non-qualifying book but avoid cancel churn. At expiry, cancel and sweep
every adding order. If q is nonzero, retain or restore only the aggregate-capped
reducer. A fresh complete qualifying book resets the episode; an incomplete,
stale, quarantined, or rejected frame cannot.

Acceptance covers just below/at/above the duration, transient recovery, both
position signs, flat and non-flat markets, existing in-flight/unknown adding
orders, cancel ambiguity, a clock step, disconnect generation changes, and no
resumption from stale truth. Add a composed owner test and a compiling mutation
whose deterministic catcher proves the configured duration reaches its final
consumer.

Codex was out of quota, so the loop's audit/challenge/adjudicate was run offline
with two independent non-codex reviewer threads plus operator adjudication. Note
the independence caveat: both reviewers were Claude-family, so this is
different-model independence, NOT the cross-vendor independence codex supplies.
Every citation below was re-verified by the operator against the source.

The GREEN full gate of iteration 26 was TRUE BUT NOT SUFFICIENT. Seven steps and
287 mutations passed while a blocking regression sat in the change, because no
test covered disconnect-with-inventory or pre-snapshot evaluation, and both new
SETTLING tests inject a clean orders walk BEFORE the replacement leg is sized.
A mutation catalogue can only kill code the tests exercise.

--- D1. BLOCKING REGRESSION. FIXED 2026-08-19. ---

The recap predicate had no target > 0 guard, and target is legitimately 0:

  fundedReducer returns 0 on a nil book OR empty levels (run.go, the levels.Max
  !ok branch). SizesFor sets HasReduce unconditionally for any q != 0 while
  SizeR caps Reduce at funded (skew.go), so wanted stays TRUE and target is 0 --
  the !wanted branch never sees it. The predicate then degenerates to
  atRisk(side) > 0 and cancels ANY resting exit, including a compliant one.

Reachability, traced end to end and then reproduced in a test:
  ApplyDisconnect sets ResetBooks: !clean, so an ABNORMAL close calls
  core.Rig.ResetOnReconnect, which empties every level. The owner loop runs
  evaluate and pump after EVERY select arm including the event arm, so evaluate
  executes immediately with empty books. The recap sits deliberately ABOVE the
  !actionable guard, so its cancel leg dispatches from a book nothing may be
  placed against, and Conditions.Valid then holds the replacement until
  resnapshot. Same collapse at startup with adopted inventory, before the first
  snapshot lands.

Net pre-fix behaviour: on every abnormal disconnect while holding inventory, the
harness DELETED its own correctly-sized exit at the moment it went blind, and
could not replace it until reconnect and resnapshot. That is the exact inversion
of I1 ("no stop path may stop reducing risk") and A4, both of which this unit's
own comments cite. SizeR's doc says an unfundable reducer is "not placed"; the
change silently promoted that to "cancel the one you have".

This was a REGRESSION, not a pre-existing hazard: HEAD has zero
KindCancelConfirmPlace enqueue sites and no cancelConfirmed field at all, so the
entire branch is new. lip-732 also introduces the FIRST activation of the
cancel-confirm-place machinery in quote/queue.go, which was dead code until now.

The in-code comment asserting this "fires on genuine overshoot alone, never on a
compliant exit" was false at target = 0. It has been corrected in place.

FIX APPLIED: guard the predicate on target > 0. Given q != 0, target is 0
exactly when funded is 0 -- either the book is unreadable or capital is
exhausted -- and cancelling the exit is wrong in BOTH cases. Overshoot that
cannot yet be replaced is strictly safer than no exit at all.

TEST ADDED: TestAnAbnormalDisconnectDoesNotCancelTheCompliantExit in
gate_failure_test.go. The exit is sized at EXACTLY the quantized |q|, so the
only thing that can produce a reducing-side cancel is the target collapse; the
clean-close case is the control, and there is a pre-disconnect control assertion
so nothing is attributable to the fixture. Verified to FAIL on both abnormal
cases with the guard reverted and PASS with it restored. build, vet and every
harness package pass with the fix.

--- D2. CONFIRMED, STILL OPEN. Hand to the next round. ---

The replacement leg of the cancel-confirm-place is deterministically unbuildable
in production timing, so the designed confirm-then-place mechanism never
actually operates.

applyWriteResult on Absent calls ConfirmAbsent and sets cancelConfirmed but does
NOT touch pf.LiveOrders. restingOn never consults cancelConfirmed. The same loop
iteration then runs pump: the place leg is released, dequeues, and build calls
targetSize, where remainder = target - atRisk(side) and atRisk still counts the
just-cancelled order. remainder clamps to 0, build errors with "the side is
already carrying its aggregate target", the intents are dropped and a
WRITE_NOT_BUILDABLE SEV2 is raised. Recovery is the fallback path only: the next
complete walk clears LiveOrders and the latch, then decideSide places a fresh
KindPlace.

Cost per recap: one spurious SEV2, and the reducing side ABSENT from the book
for up to position_poll_s rather than the documented single dispatch cycle. The
in-code comment claiming build "sizes the remainder against the shrunken
aggregate" is false at dispatch time.

The two new SETTLING tests structurally step over this window: both inject the
clean walk BEFORE the replacement is sized, then assert the replacement does not
dispatch, and hand-reset the latch. No test in the suite builds the replacement
in the stale-LiveOrders window that production always occupies.

Not fixed here because the repair is a design decision, not a typo: the
defensible fix is to let restingOn discount quantity on a side where
cancelConfirmed is true (ConfirmAbsent is, after all, a complete verifying read
showing absence), but that trades against H-FAIL-3's rule of counting an order
until the exchange confirms it gone. That judgment is worth codex's independent
read rather than an operator's.

MISSING TEST for D2: a production-timing SETTLING case with NO manufactured
post-Absent walk, asserting the place leg acks at 1 contract with zero
WRITE_NOT_BUILDABLE anomalies.

--- D3. NOTED, NOT VERIFIED, LOW WEIGHT. ---

Possible recap churn when a reducer partial fill lands in the orders-then-
positions fetch window: q shrinks before LiveOrders.Remaining does, so atRisk
briefly exceeds target on a healthy at-touch exit. The reviewer conceded the
directive's "possibly-live quantity above target" arguably endorses firing here.
The operator did NOT independently verify the poller ordering claim. Treat as a
churn cost to weigh, not an established defect.

A composite involving stale Intent.Role on a released StageSecond place leg plus

title: F8/H-QUE-3: 429 recovery with reserved P1 dispatch
description:
Implement F8 for reads, creates, and cancels. A 429 is neither a definite
create rejection nor proof that a cancel failed; preserve ownership and maximum
possibly-live quantity, requeue safely, halve the effective write rate,
exponentially back off with jitter, restore after 60 seconds clean, and emit
SEV2 after 60 seconds sustained.

Backoff must not sleep while owning a dispatcher slot. Reverse the current
one-worker cut: retain one dispatch authority but run a bounded transport pool
with at least one slot reserved for P1 reducers, as H-QUE-3 requires. Keep
capital reservation atomic across workers and prove a hard upper bound from P1
readiness to network dispatch under an unbounded coalesced-cancel storm,
repeated 429s, and one hung non-reserved request.

Acceptance covers 429 on every REST method, Retry-After if present and malformed,
rate halve/restore, jitter bounds, cancellation during backoff, request timeout,
P0/P1 fairness, no duplicate coid, no false cancel absence, and no lost intent.
Add composed scenario coverage and compiling mutations for status
misclassification, immutable rate, sleeping worker, and reducer starvation.

title: Implementer can end its turn waiting on a background task, and the loop scores it as success
description:
Loop iteration 26's implement turn ended after 34 minutes having returned 297
bytes:

  "The Monitor is armed and the background gate task will also notify me on
  completion. My implementation work is done and locally verified; I'm now
  waiting on the authoritative quick-gate run before giving the final report.
  I'll report the gate result (verbatim if it fails) as soon as it completes."

The implementer armed a background watcher and ended its turn expecting to be
woken. It is invoked as a single non-interactive "claude -p" run, so ending the
turn ends the run and nothing wakes it. No gate result was ever reported.

WHY THIS IS NOT COSMETIC. run_claude treats any non-empty result as success --
the "implement failed after retries" guard only fires when the value is None. So
a turn that quits early while claiming it will report later is indistinguishable
from a completed one, and the conductor goes straight on to spend roughly six
hours on the authoritative full gate. On this occasion the code happened to be
complete and the gate came back GREEN, but nothing in the loop checked that. A
turn that ended the same way with HALF the work done would have consumed the
same six hours and a round.

The implement report is written to NN-implement.md for the operator; the audit
template is fed the directive, the diff and the gate output rather than the
report, so a missing report degrades the operator's audit trail rather than the
audit itself. The scheduling cost is the real damage.

FIX. loop/protocol/implement.md should state plainly that the run is single-shot
and that the turn must not end while waiting on anything: run loop/gates.sh
--quick to completion inside the turn, block on the result, and put the observed
outcome in the final message. Worth considering a conductor-side guard as well,
since the prompt is advice and this failure mode is silent -- for example
rejecting a result that is implausibly short, or that contains no gate outcome,
in the same way ALREADY_SATISFIED is verified rather than trusted.

implement.md is hash-pinned in conductor.py CONTROL_FILES, so changing it is an
operator action requiring a re-pin of st["control"].
acceptance_criteria: An implement turn that ends without a gate outcome is not accepted as a successful implementation. implement.md states the run is single-shot and the turn must not end while waiting on a background task.

title: Add a negative-control mutation for the gateStopped-restricted reducer aggregate check
description:

title: Negative control attributes any suite flake to the mutation in flight
description:
The negative control decides whether a mutation was caught from the exit status
of ONE "go test -count=1" run across all of PKGS (harness_negative_control.py,
the run/evaluate block in main). The catcher names come from parsing which tests
failed in that same output. So a flaky test anywhere in PKGS is attributed to
whichever mutation happened to be in flight, and for a row expected to be inert
the flake is reported as NOT INERT.

Observed 2026-08-15 on loop iteration 24 (lip-732 round 1). The full gate went
RED on exactly one of 287 mutations: M26 NOT INERT, naming
TestSEV2IsLimitedPerClassMarketAndReportsSuppression. M26 cannot be caught by
anything. It rewrites q == 0 as q.Float() == 0.0 in Qty.IsFlat, where Qty is
int64 (num/qty.go:37), QtyScale is 100 (:20) and Float is float64(q)/QtyScale
(:130). At q = 0 both forms are true; at any q != 0 the magnitude of float64(q)
is at least 1, so the quotient is at least 0.01 and both forms are false. The
two expressions agree on every representable Qty, so no test can distinguish
them and no code change can make the mutation observable. Verified empirically
as well: the named test passes under the mutation, and the whole harness/ping
package passes 12 of 12 mutated runs plus one under -race.

Cost of a spurious row: the authoritative gate is about six hours, and the
conductor debits a unit's round before launching (conductor.py, the round debit
just after unit selection), so one flake costs six hours and one of a unit's
three rounds, and sends the adjudicator's repair instruction after a defect that
does not exist. At 287 mutations times one run each, a per-run flake rate of a
few tenths of a percent yields roughly one spurious row per gate.

MITIGATED, NOT FIXED. A confirm-rerun now re-runs any mutation whose outcome
disagrees with the catalogue and records the disagreement only if it reproduces,
reporting the flap rather than swallowing it. That removes the false verdict but
leaves the flaky test in place.

LEAD. harness/ping/stub_test.go awaitHealthy waits out the store's real retry
ladder against a 30-second WALL-CLOCK deadline. Under the load of a 287x
full-suite sweep that is exactly the kind of bound that breaks; it passes
comfortably on an idle machine, which is why 28 unmutated local runs did not
reproduce it. Not confirmed as the culprit -- the failing run's output was not
retained, which is itself worth fixing.

BEARING ON THE PROMOTION GATE. lip-8hn.1 requires the complete catalogue green
with no survivor, did-not-build, wrong catcher or unexplained inert result. An
oracle that emits about one spurious row per run cannot certify that criterion,
so this arguably belongs as a dependency of lip-8hn.1 rather than merely
adjacent to it. Left for the operator to decide.
acceptance_criteria: A flaky test elsewhere in PKGS can no longer change a mutation's recorded verdict, and the flake itself is identified and fixed rather than only re-run. A full gate reports zero flaps on an otherwise green tree.

title: Programs() refuses volume-type incentive programmes; one active volume programme stops the harness booting
description:
MEASURED 2026-08-12 by go/cmd/conform. The /incentive_programs endpoint carries 137,616 records: 115,298 of incentive_type 'liquidity', ALL of which have target_size_fp, and 22,318 of incentive_type 'volume', NONE of which do. rest.Client.Programs (read.go:655-657) refuses any record without target_size_fp -- 'the Target Size is Qualifies()'s threshold and there is no defensible default for it' -- and the walk is first-error-wins, so ONE such record fails the whole walk.

runtime.go:328-334 turns that into a refusal to start: 'reading the active LIP universe: the walk %s after %d pages'. So this is a boot failure, not a degradation.

NOT FIRING TODAY, AND THAT IS THE ONLY REASON IT IS NOT P0. Production sends status=active (read.go:631-632), and the active set today is 3,276 records, all liquidity, all with target_size_fp -- conform measured 0 refusals against exactly what production reads. === 2026-08-11, RESCOPED by lip-7u4's final adjudication (codex directive) ===

resnapshot, RECONCILE_NOW and an uptime record." That framing is WRONG, and it
understates the defect by one whole category.

and :140, Downtime at :152). There is no caller in cmd/harness and no caller
anywhere else in the module. Nothing constructs it, so `Observe` is never

idle-sleeps. A sleep gap silently biases every rate, every uptime figure and
every realised-vs-predicted comparison measured across it, and F7 exists for
exactly that. The operator currently works around it with a detached

that is present in the source and absent from the process.

PRESERVE THE F7 RESPONSE EXACTLY AS SPECIFIED -- SEV2 HOST_SLEEP_OR_STALL,
forced resnapshot, RECONCILE_NOW, and the downtime interval recorded as uptime

title: H-CLOSE-1: stop adding when the ticker leaves the active LIP programme set
description:
cmd/harness/run.go passes quote.MarketInput.ProgramEnded=false unconditionally, with the reasoning at the call site.

H-CLOSE-1: at end_date there is no reward left to earn, so the adding quote has no purpose; the reducing quote stays and is now genuinely free.

The naive read -- program.end_date from /incentive_programs -- is WRONG. Live universe 2026-08-07: LIP programmes are short REWARD PERIODS inside a market's life. Sampled programme KXSILVER15M-26AUG071800-00 ran start_date 21:45Z -> end_date 22:00Z on a market whose close_time was 22:00Z, while 180 of 200 active programmes sit on markets closing >24h out. So end_date passing is a gap between periods, not the end of the incentive.

The correct condition is membership: this ticker is in no active programme any more. That is a poll of /incentive_programs?status=active (public, unsigned) plus a membership test, on roughly the schedule_poll_s cadence. feed.Universe cannot answer it -- it returns {ticker: target_size} and a ticker order, and go/feed is hash-pinned.

Cost of leaving it: economic, not safety. false keeps the adding quote alive, so the failure is quoting while unpaid. Every rule bounding real exposure is wired (close lead, the operator early-close backoff, inventory ladder, gate, capital caps). The opposite error is worse: reading a between-periods gap as programme-ended stops quoting in a market that is still paying.

title: Read-only qualification: 4-6h real process, zero writes
description:
Run the real one-market process for a supervised 4–6 hour operating window with H-VER-1 unarmed. This is a read-only operational qualification, not the promotion gate for the later writer. It proves that the nominated commit can observe the real account, restart from its durable paths, remain monitored, and expose every attempted write without any network non-GET call.

Use the actual launchd/caffeinate supervision, five-record store, alert channel and external dead man. Force at least one websocket disconnect/quarantine/reconnect/resnapshot/reconcile and one process death/restart using the same durable paths. A safely forced event may discover and fail a missing relay; q01 does not require unrelated exchange write-response behavior to be implemented before the observer is allowed to run.

Owner-only stall and exchange schedule/host-clock jump remain deterministic promotion scenarios, not q01 live drills. The production binary has no safe external mechanism to freeze one goroutine or make the exchange change its schedule, and changing the host clock is not a defensible real-account test. q01 still exercises ordinary schedule polling and proves the real monitor/heartbeat paths continue.

Require at least 99% monitor availability against elapsed-time cadence, fresh complete position/order/fill walks, continuing heartbeat in every reached global state, bounded durable would-write and attempted-method evidence, and no silent anomaly loss. Preserve the compact qualification bundle.

No agent executes this bead against the real account. Live-account execution, forced external events and alarm confirmation are operator actions.
acceptance_criteria:
Attach start/end timestamps, exact commit and config hash, actual transport method counts measured below the write guard, attempted methods measured above it, disconnect/reconnect/reconcile timestamps, state/anomaly summary, monitor/portfolio freshness evidence, committed-run restart linkage, bounded would-write episodes, heartbeat/dead-man check-in evidence, and proof that the external missed-heartbeat alarm fired.

The assessor requires at least four hours of linked monotonic active time; the operator plans an orderly end by six hours. Running long does not retroactively falsify safety evidence, so six hours is an operating cutoff rather than a qualification loophole or a machine failure condition. Any network non-GET call, unexplained SEV1, anomaly-drop evidence, cadence-adjusted monitor ratio below 99%, incomplete/stale portfolio coverage, missed heartbeat, incomplete adoption/reconciliation, corrupt evidence bundle, unlinked segment, or unbounded local reservation/evidence growth fails qualification. The complete mutation catalogue must be green on the exact nominated commit before the operator starts it.
notes:
Candidate identity for the q01 attempt (prepared 2026-08-12, not yet started).

  nominated commit  dc77e3f  (the commit lip-jy4 closed GREEN, 273/273)
  binary            /Users/hugh/.lip/bin/harness
  binary sha256     1882b82fbec9c00aeb683086fb2d1e11a86cbcd7fff0462b96dfba3fdd8d0cf1

BINARY IDENTITY IS THE SHA256 ALONE. This repo's module lives in go/ while the
git root is one level up, and under that layout Go emits no vcs.revision /
vcs.modified build setting even when -buildvcs=true is passed explicitly --
verified, no error and no stamp. So currentBinaryIdentity()
(cmd/harness/qualification.go:144) appends nothing to the hash. Two consequences
worth recording here rather than rediscovering later:

  - The dirty working tree at build time (.beads/interactions.jsonl modified,
    .codex-handoff/ untracked) could not have contaminated the evidence bundle.
    That risk does not exist under this layout.
  - The commit linkage is an operator assertion, not a self-attestation by the
    binary -- but it is checkable, because the build is deterministic. Checking
    out dc77e3f to /Users/hugh/kek/lip-q01-build and running
    `go build -o <out> ./cmd/harness` from go/ under go1.26.4 reproduces
    1882b82f... byte for byte; two independent builds already did. The path
    matters: without -trimpath the build directory is embedded.

CONFIG. Byte-identical to the reviewed config.example.json apart from `ticker`,
so the template's "a diff of the file against an empty one is the whole config
review" property holds. s=1 canary, so no -rung flag is required (main.go:370).

TICKER SELECTION. The active LIP universe is 3,245 markets across 4 pages.
score.py, q1select.py and the lip.db collector all read ONE page of 200 with no
cursor, so every view built on them is truncated; cmd/harness does a complete
cursor walk (harness/rest/read.go:630) and refuses to start on a ticker outside
the complete set. Membership was therefore re-tested against the complete walk,
which KXMAMDANIMENTION-26AUG12-SAFE passes. A lip.db-based reading that showed
this ticker present in only 17 of 61 recent snapshots was a paging artifact, not
a membership lapse.

The hazard the choice is made against is a programme lapsing ACROSS THE MANDATED
RESTART DRILL: every restart re-runs the active-programme walk, and a ticker that
has fallen out by then turns KeepAlive:true into a respawn loop against a start
refusal, with the run dead and nothing reporting it. This ticker's programme end
and market close are both 2026-09-03T14:00Z -- 22 days of runway, so neither can
fire inside a 4-6h window. Book traffic is not a qualification risk: the monitor
ticks at 1 Hz unconditionally (cmd/harness/monitor.go:65), so slot freshness
comes from the harness's own cadence and not from market activity.

TWO OPERATING TRAPS recorded before the run rather than after:

  - The restart drill must SIGKILL the harness CHILD, by pid. The launchd job's
    argv is `/usr/bin/caffeinate -is <harness> ...`
    (harness/lifecycle/launchd.go:125), so caffeinate is the process launchd
    tracks and harness is its child. `pkill -f harness` matches both, and
    SIGKILLing caffeinate orphans a still-running harness while launchd starts a

    is also wrong: it sets WINDING_DOWN and commits a durable stop
    (main.go:300-307), which would make the rest of the window a wind-down
    rather than an observation.
  - paths.stop cannot end the run. It is Section 12's out-of-band halt and
    explicitly not a drain (config.go:148-161): it stops the harness adding and

Editing the config or rebuilding the binary between deploy and assessment makes
every restart fail with ErrMetadataMismatch (harness/qual/recorder.go:307),
which under KeepAlive is a silent respawn loop. Nothing changes mid-run.

Start was blocked by lip-83o: LaunchdPlan.Render() writes booleans as <true></true> and launchd rejects that form with 'Bootstrap failed: 5: Input/output error', so -deploy's plist has never been loadable. Isolated by single-variable probe agents; only the tag form predicts the failure. Working around it operator-side in ~/.lip/q01.sh, which runs plutil -convert xml1 over the installed plist before bootstrapping and asserts no paired booleans remain. The conversion is semantics-preserving -- ProgramArguments verified byte-identical across it -- so the deployed argv is still exactly what installAgent wrote, and the run's identity is unaffected. No Go was edited, so the mutation catalogue that closed lip-jy4 against dc77e3f still holds.
ATTEMPT 1 ABORTED 2026-08-12T17:33Z after ~3 minutes, on lip-9tr. Portfolio slots read observed 12 / fresh_complete 0 / incomplete_walks 12 while monitor slots were a clean 60/60, so the local bar was already unreachable and six hours would only have produced a guaranteed failure. Cause is real exchange data: fill 1582884a-1f64-7c20-fab4-b40468ad5df6 carries fee_cost "0.017200", six decimals, and portfolio.go:564 parses fee_cost with rest.ParsePrice4, whose measured quantum is 1e-4 dollars. convertFills errors, FILL_UNCONVERTIBLE SEV1 fires, the whole walk is discarded and the fills freshness clock does not advance -- once per 5s poll, permanently, because the fill is historical and appears in every complete walk. No operational workaround exists. The alert path worked correctly throughout: the SEV1 was delivered to the operator's phone with urgent priority within seconds, alongside the STARTUP summary and a SEV2 RESNAPSHOT_DEFERRED.

title: FromWire is dead code while its doc claims it guards 7.5 adoption
description:
rest/wire.go:59-71. FromWire enforces the 1..99 cent bound (quote.MinPrice/MaxPrice) and its doc comment at wire.go:55-58 says it is used for reading resting orders back off the exchange for 7.5 adoption. It is referenced only from wire_test.go: decodeOrder and readPrice never call it.

CONSEQUENCE: the read path imposes no 1..99 bound at all, so a resting order the exchange reports at 0c or 100c near settlement decodes cleanly today. Whether that bound SHOULD apply on the read path is the open question -- the adoption path arguably wants it and the doc says it has it.

WHY IT IS WORTH A BEAD RATHER THAN A SHRUG: this tree already names this exact shape as a recurring failure. runtime.go:307-311 describes the two BYPASS mutations as leaving F6 'implemented, tested, and on no path the harness actually uses -- which is the shape H-CAP-8 has already had once in this tree'. A tested-but-unreachable guard is worse than no guard, because the test reports coverage of a path production does not take.

RESOLVE ONE OF THREE WAYS, deliberately: wire it into the read path if the bound belongs there; delete it and drop the doc claim if it does not; or keep it with the comment corrected to say it is unused and why. Leaving it as-is is the only option that is definitely wrong.

title: go/cmd/conform: the read-only conformance sweep
description:
ADDED 2026-08-12. A read-only prober that walks every endpoint in rest.client.go's Endpoint table with the real credentials and pushes every record through the harness's OWN decoders, one record at a time.

WHY IT IS NOT scripts/pagecontract.py: that script is pure Python and reimplements cursor-walking and decoding itself, so it cannot exercise the Go decoders and has no seam to be extended at. It measures the WIRE contract; this measures our READING of it.

THE ISOLATION IS THE POINT. Every decoder in rest is first-error-wins by design -- correct for production, where a partly-understood walk must not replace state, and useless for discovery, because it reports record 0 and hides records 1..N. conform walks with the real transport (Client.Walk, so pagination and rewind defects still surface), then replays each raw record through the real typed decoder ALONE by handing it back through a Doer that answers with a synthetic one-record page. Same decoder, only the batch boundary moves.

READ-ONLY IS STRUCTURAL: getOnly sits above the transport and refuses any non-GET before a socket is touched, mirroring pagecontract.py's dry_run=True.

FILTERS MUST MATCH PRODUCTION. The first run walked /incentive_programs unfiltered and reported 22,318 refusals; production sends status=active and sees none of them. The probe table now carries per-probe filters, and a probe that deliberately walks wider is marked 'latent' so its refusals are reported as risk rather than as a live defect. Anyone extending this must keep that distinction -- it is the difference between a finding and a fabrication.

NOT GATED: loop/gates.sh scopes vet/gofmt/test-race to ./harness/... and ./cmd/harness/..., so this package is only compiled by 'go build ./...'. It is a diagnostic instrument and must never be imported by the harness.

FIRST RUN found: 0 refusals against everything production reads (fills, orders, both position arrays, the 3,276 active programmes, balance); fee_cost is 1e-6 on all 15 fills; 8 fills would trip TAKER_FILL; the volume-programme boot hazard (lip-44s); and the 'finalized' status SEV1 (lip-t4n). It also cleared four candidate defects that would otherwise have been guessed at.
notes:
TAPE MODE ADDED and run 2026-08-12. conform -rest=false -tapes <paths> streams recorded tapes through go/tape and pushes every frame through wsx.InspectFrame, which is the pure part of the wsx decode surface -- raw bytes in, classification out, no socket. This is the answer to "replay the tapes through the harness wsx handling"; go/cmd/replay is NOT that entry point, since it drives the frozen lip/core, lip/store and lip/tape trio instead.

RESULT ACROSS FOUR TAPES, ~4.8M real recorded frames:
  testdata/gate-tape.jsonl.gz               410,375 frames
  archive/raw-20260724T225527Z.jsonl.gz     410,422 frames
  raw-20260724T231211Z.jsonl.gz             2,000,000 sampled of a 7.1GB live tape
  shadow/raw-20260725T054112Z.jsonl.gz      2,000,000 sampled of a 6.5GB tape
  UNDELIVERABLE: 0.  GRANULARITY VIOLATIONS: 0.  In all four.

So H-CO-3a is not being violated by real traffic -- no resting book price is a non-integer cent anywhere in the sample -- and there is no frame wsx would refuse to pass to core. The websocket decode surface is clean, in contrast to the REST fee surface.

ONE FALSE POSITIVE WAS FOUND AND FIXED IN THIS TOOL, recorded because the next person will hit it. The first run reported exactly 1 FRAME_UNDECODABLE per large tape, with an empty example. It was not a defect: tape.Envelope carries a Universe field alongside M, and an envelope may legitimately carry no frame bytes at all. Pushing those through InspectFrame manufactures a FRAME_UNDECODABLE no real consumer would ever see. sweepTape now counts them as envelopes_without_frame and does not judge them; the count is 1 per 2M in the sampled tapes.

That is the second time filters/inputs wider than production produced a fabricated finding in this tool -- the first was walking /incentive_programs without status=active. Anyone extending conform should assume the default is wrong until it is checked against what production actually sends.

title: §15: restore 60s balance-poll telemetry
description:
Adjudicated in lip-7u4 (2026-08-11) under a codex directive. `cfg.Params.BalancePoll`
(harness/cfg/params.go:56, default 60s at :134) is DECLARED AND NEVER CONSUMED --
there is no periodic balance-poll loop anywhere in cmd/harness. The only
production balance read in the module is a single startup call,
`s.src.Balance(ctx)` at harness/lifecycle/startup.go:673, seeding the capital
model (adopt.go:83,122,164-165). `balance_poll` is listed among hstore's
`deferredTables` (harness/hstore/schema.go:53-56, "§15 tables the pilot cut ...
DEFERRED, not forgotten").

WHY THIS IS NOT A SAFETY DEFECT, and therefore not CR-1-blocking.
Unlike `position_poll_s` -- which backs H-POS-1's authoritative overwrite and
H-POS-2's drift ladder -- `balance_poll_s` has NO independent safety or
freshness rule anywhere in the spec. Its sole stated purpose is §15 payout
observation: spec:1780 gives the row as "every 60s | the payout is observable
only as a balance delta". pilot-plan.md:110 defers it explicitly, alongside
`position_poll`, `snap` and `uptime`, while insisting "deleting a table does not
delete the fact that must be proved". So the unread parameter is deferred
TELEMETRY, not a dead consumer in the class of lip-lqw (inv_kill), lip-2da
(stuck_s), lip-gp8 (pnl_kill) or lip-lpf (H-CAP-8).

SCOPE: a periodic balance poll at `balance_poll_s`, writing the `balance_poll`
row of §15's table, plus whatever compact evidence the qualification runner
needs in place of the dense table.

HARD CONSTRAINT -- read this before implementing.
The balance delta MUST NOT feed H-HALT-5's pnl. H-HALT-5 (spec:1613-1641) pins
pnl to a fills-and-cost-basis definition PRECISELY BECAUSE a balance-delta
reading is the one an arriving LIP reward corrupts: red-team HR-021 records two
conforming implementations disagreeing completely, where "an incoming $100 LIP
reward masks the drawdown entirely". Rewards, deposits and withdrawals are
excluded from pnl by definition. This bead restores the observation channel for
the payout; it does not create a second, wrong route into the loss floor.

NOT CR-1-BLOCKING. Do not add it as a dependency of lip-9j3, lip-q01 or lip-jy4.

title: The scale rung permits an S that H-CAP-8 now refuses at its own described capital
description:
Now that risk.CheckFundable runs at startup (lip-lpf, aa12067), the `scale` rung
in cmd/harness/config.go describes a configuration the capital rule forbids.

  rungs["scale"] = maxS 100, human: "6 markets, larger S, $500 -- ONLY after a
  real payout is observed"

At the 6 markets and $500 that string names, with §16's capital_reserve = 0.25:

  deployable = $500 * 0.75 = $375
  6 markets * S * $0.99 <= $375  =>  S <= 63

So the rung's own cap of S=100 costs 6 * 100 * $0.99 = $594 and is refused by
CheckFundable at every start. The largest S that actually loads at scale's
described sizing is 63, not 100.

This is the lip-afr / HR-005 class reached from a third direction: a table whose
recommended step cannot be started. Before lip-lpf it was latent because nothing
consulted fundability; the check is now live, so the rung table and the capital
model disagree in a way an operator meets as a refusal.

NOT URGENT: scale is the last ladder step and is gated on a real payout being
observed first, so nothing on the current pilot path touches it. The other three
rungs are clear -- canary 1*1*$0.99, pilot 1*12*$0.99 = $11.88 and second
2*12*$0.99 = $23.76 all sit inside $75 deployable at the default capital_max.

DECIDE, DO NOT ASSUME: the fix is either to lower scale's maxS to 63, to raise
the capital_max its human string names, or to record that the rung caps S alone
and its prose is advisory. That is a spec question about what the ladder step
MEANS, not a code change to make silently.

Found while closing lip-lpf; not by a directed audit of the rung table.

title: F21 partial: the general deadline recompute after a clock step is unproven
description:
lip-7u4 pass 1 classified F21 PROVEN_WIRED for the close-lead half only.

PROVEN: M-3AF-STALESCHED is caught by the composed TestAnUnknownCloseStopsAddingAndLeavesTheExitAlive, and M-HS-STALLCLOCK by TestWriterStallUsesMonotonicTime.

UNPROVEN: F21's actual clause is 'recompute ALL deadlines from the new wall clock; never let a step skip a close lead'. Only the close lead is observed. The other wall-clock deadlines -- drain timeout, heartbeat, unresolved-fill escalation at 120s, the 1800s stuck timer, alert rate-limit buckets -- have no composed test showing them recomputed across a step.

OBSERVABLE: a composed run whose wall clock steps forward and whose deadlines are all rebased, asserted on at least the drain timeout and the heartbeat alongside the close lead.
notes:
=== 2026-08-10, lip-7u4 audit: F21 is safe TODAY, but incidentally ===
Detection half is dead: F21 shares F7's lifecycle.SleepDetector, which has zero
production callers, so HOST_SLEEP_OR_STALL never fires and there is no
recompute-on-step logic anywhere.

The spec's critical EFFECT -- "never let a step skip a close lead" -- nonetheless
holds, for a reason unrelated to F21: o.untilClose() (cmd/harness/run.go:863-868)
calls time.Until(o.closeAt) FRESH EVERY TICK against the live wall clock instead
of caching a computed deadline, and the write budget refills on monotonic elapsed
(dispatch.go:519). A clock step is therefore absorbed rather than skipped.

So this bead's "unproven" is accurate but understates the fragility: the property
is currently guaranteed by the ABSENCE of caching, not by any logic that would
survive someone adding a cached deadline as an optimisation. Recommend the
composed test assert the property AND that a mutation introduce a cached
deadline, so the protection stops being incidental.

title: SPEC PATCH: reconcile stale post-red-team clauses
description:
The SHA-pinned harness spec contains post-red-team clauses that cannot all be
implemented literally. This is an operator-only dedicated spec-patch unit; an
ordinary implementation turn must not edit notes/harness-spec.md.

Reconcile these stale contradictions without changing the already-tested
canonical behaviour:

1. H-ORD-2/H-ORD-4a/F12/A10/V4.11 say an ambiguous create is never retried,
   while H-ORD-2b requires same-coid retry up to three times after measured 409
   deduplication. Canonical rule: retry only the identical coid and byte-identical
   payload; never a new coid; unresolved remains UNKNOWN.
2. F19 says keep trading and use an on-disk journal, while H-STORE-3 says a
   persistence failure stops adding and explicitly rejects disk journal as a
   disk-failure fallback. H-STORE-3's later rule wins.
3. H-TOP-4 gives hstore to owner, while H-STORE-2 requires a dedicated writer.
   The topology table must name the dedicated writer.
4. V4.2 says a clean-disconnect book is retained, while H-FAIL-5 requires every
   disconnected book to remain non-actionable until resnapshot plus portfolio
   reconciliation. Diagnostic retention is permitted; actionability is not.
5. The header calls close_lead_keep_reducing unresolved, while §§9, 16, and 19
   set it true on argument. The header must reflect the recorded resolution.

rules and current production tests, update the pinned checksum through the

title: requote_interval_s is a dead parameter and a spec inconsistency - record, do not implement
description:
DO NOT IMPLEMENT WITHOUT A DECISION. Implementing it would be a deviation, not
a fix.

`requote_interval_s` (§16, "5.0 s/side/market", cites §6.6) occurs EXACTLY ONCE
in the whole ~2300-line spec: its own §16 table row.
- §6.6, the section it cites, defines the P0-P4 priority queue, the
  anti-starvation promotion, and a GLOBAL write-rate bucket. It never mentions a
  per-side minimum interval.
- §6.5, the actual requote policy, bounds requoting with H-Q-6 (only requote
  when the reference moves against us), H-Q-7 (250ms debounce on the new touch
  HOLDING) and H-Q-8 (stranded brake). It never mentions it either.
- Every other requote-adjacent §16 row traces to a numbered rule
  (debounce_s -> H-Q-7, stale_bid_ticks -> H-Q-8) or to §6.6's own prose
  (max_queue_age, write_rate, write_burst). This is the only row in the cluster
  whose cited section does not define it.

IN CODE: cfg/params.go:47 (declaration), :127 (default 5s), plus two config
tests. `Params.Validate()` does not bounds-check it. cmd/harness's fileConfig
has no `requote_interval_s` key, so the operator cannot even set it. No runtime
path reads it.

ITS ONLY LIVE ANCESTOR is the superseded Python prototype probebot.py:430,
where the identically-named knob WAS a real per-side cooldown
(`time.monotonic() - last_requote[side] >= requote_interval_s`) against a
different, now-superseded spec (notes/phase2-spec.md).

ARGUMENT AGAINST IMPLEMENTING: a 5s per-side cooldown would delay H-Q-8's
stranded-brake snap-back, which §6.5 says to perform "regardless of which
direction it moved". The spec's own stated rate-control mechanism is H-Q-7's
250ms debounce, chosen with an explicit argument about order rate.

WHAT DOES BOUND REQUOTE RATE TODAY: H-Q-7's 250ms condition-persistence
debounce (per side), and the global write bucket (write_rate 5/s, burst 10,
shared across every market, side and write reason). Neither is a per-(market,
side) minimum spacing. Note harness-spec.md is SHA-pinned, and
cfg/params_test.go asserts the §16 table field-for-field, so the FIELD must
stay whatever is decided about the behaviour.

title: RED-TEAM FIRST (do not implement): depth-depletion requote hypothesis
description:
STATUS: UNEXAMINED HYPOTHESIS. Not approved, not scheduled, not designed.

DO NOT IMPLEMENT. DO NOT FLESH OUT. The next action on this bead is a RED TEAM
whose job is to KILL the idea, not to plan it. Only if it survives that does
anyone discuss whether it is worth designing. Filed at the operator's request in
exactly those terms.

--- THE IDEA, VERBATIM (Hugh, 2026-08-06) ---

(1) "also can you make note of something I have been thinking of directionally,
of course there is an order book and we are likely placing orders at the most
competitive price, but may not be first in queue, in some instances it will be
impossible for us to anctipate being filled, but if we can detect orders in front
of us being filled or momentum in orders being filled, we can cancel and move our
resting orders, I do not know if this is already part of the plan, make some note
of it to be investigated later after the current to do work is done"

(2) "well if we do not know queue position but we do know the volume of orders at
our price, we can set a threshold in which if we are not filled before, the
threshold being a portion-al decrease in the number of resting orders at our
price, and then a set wait time before requoting to see if market will move"

--- WHAT THE RED TEAM MUST TRY TO ESTABLISH ---

Each of these is a way the idea DIES. The red team's success condition is proving
one of them, not surveying them.

R1. The signal is not observable well enough to act on. Our own resting size must
    be subtracted from the level (quote/external.go OverSubtracted documents that
    our OWN fill leaves the book before the fill report arrives, so the model
    claims size the book no longer shows). Delta loss and resync gaps compound
    it. If depth-at-our-price is only approximately known, a proportional
    threshold on it is noise.

R2. The signal does not separate informed flow from ordinary churn. Depth at a
    level falls constantly for benign reasons. Cancels and trades both reduce it
    and mean opposite things. If the base rate of benign depletion swamps the
    adverse case, the detector fires mostly on nothing.

R3. The RESPONSE is net-negative under LIP scoring even if the signal is real.
    Presence gaps are revenue (S4). harness-spec.md:478-492 already declines a
    real scoring gain -- 50.0% -> 66.7% presence by improving a tick -- BECAUSE
    the adverse selection cost more. This proposal trades in the other direction:
    it gives up presence to avoid adverse selection. The same arithmetic has to
    be run, and it may come out the same way it did there.

R4. It cannot be honestly validated. harness-spec.md:1950: "Queue position is
    explicitly unobservable and is never assumed." The V2 simulator therefore
    ENUMERATES legal fill outcomes per print and asserts over the range rather
    than producing a fill. A strategy whose whole value is about WHEN we fill
    cannot be scored in a simulator that deliberately refuses to say. If it can
    only be evaluated live, it cannot be evaluated cheaply.

R5. It strains rules already argued and settled. H-Q-3 (never take, structurally
    enforced), H-Q-9 (place-then-cancel ordering, adding side only), §6.6's
    write_rate / write_burst budget and max_queue_age, and the debounce. More
    requoting spends a rate budget that exists for a reason.

R6. It is a strategy change dressed as a safety mechanism. Everything the harness
    currently does on the quoting path is derived from a numbered rule with a
    loss attached to it. This is derived from an intuition. That asymmetry is
    itself an argument for leaving it out of the pilot entirely.

--- WHAT IS ALREADY TRUE (facts, established 2026-08-06, not an endorsement) ---

- Nothing in the trading path reads prints. wsx subscribes to the 'trade' channel
  and frame.go inspectTrade CLASSIFIES ONLY; no consumer acts on a print.
- quote.RequoteInput has no fill or trade input at all. Every requote trigger is
  "the touch moved" or "we are stranded" (H-Q-8).
- Depth at an arbitrary price IS available: core.Levels.Get(price),
  core.Book.ApplyDelta, and Book.Checkpoint/StateBefore for history.
- The awkward quantity is already computed for another rule: quote.ExternalBest
  (H-Q-10) reads the best price bid by somebody OTHER than us, with our own
  resting size subtracted.
- core/rig.go:13-40 carries a load-bearing RETRACTION: trade_through is "heavily
  enriched for genuine fills but is not causally clean", because maker-side
  self-trade prevention and a cancel landing just before a sweep both produce the
  same observation. An earlier Python version wrongly claimed it was proof.

Framing (2) avoids that retraction -- it measures depletion of our own level from
deltas rather than inferring our fill from a print -- which is why it is worth
red-teaming at all rather than dismissing.

NOTHING BELOW HAS BEEN DECIDED: threshold fraction, wait duration, whether the
response is cancel-and-move or hold, which side it applies to, or whether it
belongs in the pilot at all. Do not invent them.

title: rest: Fills() walks all account history every call; backfill_h is client-side
description: harness/rest/read.go Fills() does a COMPLETE cursor walk then filters by `since` client-side. That is correct per H-PAGE-1 clause 2 (a server-side early stop on timestamp would make the walk incomplete, and only a complete walk may replace state), and it is fine for the pilot: 15 fills on the account, one market, days. It does not scale — at a 5s poll over months the walk grows without bound. Options when it matters: (a) measure whether /portfolio/fills honours min_ts and whether a bounded read still counts as complete for its window, (b) keep a durable high-water mark in harness.db and walk only until the first already-seen fill_id, treating THAT as the completeness criterion. Neither is safe to assume; both need the V1.8a treatment (measure, record, then code).

If a group ever contained BOTH an adding-side standalone cancel (P0) and a reducing-side cancel-confirm-place first leg (P1, H-QUE-2), the single DELETE would go out at P0 with the bucket bypass H-QUE-2 denies a reducing cancel. The spec does not address the case and it is unreachable from a coherent caller (a market side is either adding or reducing at one instant), so nothing was invented for it. Decide the rule and pin it, or state that it cannot occur.

acceptance_criteria: The loop runs unattended for a full night without: editing a frozen or read-only path, weakening a gate, editing harness-spec.md outside an audited spec-patch unit, or going silent. It must be stoppable by one file touch and must report its own death.
